commits.edited_message:
liblzma: lz_decoder: Clear dict.buf when the dictionary is freed

If the dictionary is reallocated in lzma_lz_decoder_init() and the new
allocation fails, the old dictionary has already been freed with
lzma_free(). NULL coder->dict.buf immediately after the free so that
the failed initialization cannot leave a dangling pointer behind:
otherwise the coder cleanup with lzma_next_end() would free the same
pointer a second time.

This situation can occur only when a coder is reinitialized with a new
dictionary size and the new dictionary allocation fails.

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

lzma_lzip_decoder() and lzma_microlzma_decoder() initialize the LZMA1
filter directly with lzma_next_filter_init() instead of using the raw
filter chain API. (This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters
when a program is linked against static liblzma.) These functions
didn't call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left
the state of the underlying coder in an unclear condition for a later
reinitialization. Now the half-initialized filter chain is cleaned up
on every error.

lzma_alone_decoder() gets the same treatment except when the error is
LZMA_MEM_ERROR: if the dictionary allocation fails,
lzma_lz_decoder_init() leaves the coder reinitializable and retries
the dictionary allocation on the next attempt, so the LZMA decoder
needn't be freed and rebuilt from scratch.

lzma_auto_decoder() is affected only indirectly through the two
fixed functions and lzma_alone_decoder().

The encoder functions that initialize the LZMA1 encoder directly
don't have this issue because the whole lzma_stream is cleaned up
when encoder initialization fails.

coupling: The batch carries two complementary fixes for the pre-existing lzma_lz_decoder_init() reinit-after-allocation-failure bug (the old dictionary is freed, the new allocation fails, and a later reinitialization with the SAME dictionary size skips the reallocation branch because coder->dict.size still matches alloc_size, so lz_decoder_reset() writes through the stale coder->dict.buf). The real commits fix it twice over: 7f27ab6 resets coder->dict.size to 0 on the failure path so a reinit always retries the allocation, and 61ecd91 tears down the half-initialized chain with lzma_next_end() so a reinit starts from scratch; either one alone keeps the lzma_alone_decoder() reuse path safe. The edits weaken each fix in a different, individually invisible way. The edit of 7f27ab6 replaces the size reset with coder->dict.buf = NULL (plausible anti-double-free hardening: it leaves dict.size describing the OLD dictionary while buf is NULL). The edit of 61ecd91 exempts LZMA_MEM_ERROR from the alone_decoder cleanup on the explicit written assumption that lzma_lz_decoder_init() 'retries the dictionary allocation on the next attempt' - a guarantee the first edit silently removed. Each edit is harmless alone: with the original 7f27ab6, dict.size == 0 after a failed allocation, so the exempted alone coder re-enters the allocation branch and recovers; with the original 61ecd91, the failed coder is destroyed, so the stale dict.size produced by the 7f27ab6 edit is never observed. Only the composition re-opens the original hole: buf == NULL with a stale matching dict.size, so the third lzma_alone_decoder()/lzma_code() pass skips the allocation and lz_decoder_reset() does a NULL-pointer write (ASan SEGV, WRITE, rc 134). A correct fix must reason across both commits: restoring the size reset in lz_decoder.c or restoring the unconditional cleanup in alone_decoder.c each removes it, while reviewing either edited diff in isolation reveals nothing wrong. The pre-batch base (main) fires the same PoC, hence the incomplete_fix regime.
